summary: Bank-only rules answer all 54 easy instances, all 5 runner records, all 4 deduplicated survivors, and 5 reproduced stored generated questions. Mathematics and native grading pass; the practice design permits bypassing the intended ODE reasoning. Package unchanged.

source_analysis.skill: Solve homogeneous first-order ODEs using y=v(x)x, reduce to x v'=F(v)-v, separate and integrate, substitute back, and select one general solution from five mathematical choices.
reasoning_steps: Recognize or use degree-zero right-hand side F(y/x).
Substitute and cancel the v term; separate the resulting variables.
Integrate using elementary powers or logarithms at easy difficulty, absorb arbitrary constants, and replace v by y/x.
Distinguish the resulting solution from plausible incorrect integrations and substitutions.
invariants: Homogeneous degree-zero first-order equation, x nonzero on an interval.
Substitution, separation, elementary integration and back-substitution remain the assessed operations.
Exactly one mathematically distinct correct solution in a five-choice radio bank.
Prompt, answer bank, worked solution and domains must describe the same equation.
permitted_variations: Change nonzero small coefficients and signs in the easy affine or cancellation families while preserving comparable integration workload.
Change the coefficient of v in affine F(v); this legitimately changes logarithmic versus power integration when crossing coefficient 1.
Change the coefficient of the surviving inverse-square term in the cubic family; derive the logarithm multiplier and root expression from it.
Vary candidate position, distractor errors and mathematically eligible solution shapes so recognizing a template or lone root does not suffice.
Power-degree variations near observed easy powers may be defensible same-method extensions, but demand workload and domain review; arbitrary new operators are not justified.

findings.description: The easy-family bank construction reveals the correct candidate without inspecting the differential equation: cube_root always has one cube-root candidate; linear_log has one candidate containing both x ln|x| and +Cx; affine always makes the smaller-magnitude linear coefficient among its two Cx^2 candidates correct. Each rule scores 18/18 across both coefficient signs. The combined rule answers the entire supplied batch and every survivor. Five stored generated questions reproduce the same defects with matching UUIDs and publisher fingerprints.

findings.reproduction: From evidence_root, run PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 /home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/.venv/bin/python reproduce_shortcut.py (expected exit 1). Minimal case: generator.generate('cube_root', 2, seed=826033), saved in minimal-failing-record.json. For y'=(2x^3+y^3)/(xy^2), select the sole cube-root candidate y=x sqrt[3](6 ln|x|+C) without reading the equation. With a=-2 the same action selects the new correct answer; the learner never needs to determine 3a. Native acceptance is retained in grader-final-results.json. Include plausible same-shape distractors requiring calculation of the surviving term and integration coefficient; vary affine distractor magnitudes so choosing the smaller one is not sufficient.
